physics_review: The fixed laboratory spinor is periodic and the finite-gap global canonical state is formed before Delta tends to infinity. The reservoir exchanges angular momentum, so the stated ensemble includes every integer laboratory Fourier sector.

For the block {|up,n-q>,|down,n>}, the lower internal spin has weights (1-cos(theta))/2 and (1+cos(theta))/2. Its limiting kinetic expectation is [(1-cos(theta))*(n-q)^2+(1+cos(theta))*n^2]/(4*I). Completing the square gives (n-q*(1-cos(theta))/2)^2/(2*I)+q^2*sin(theta)^2/(8*I), agreeing with the oracle sign and scalar term.

The finite-gap reference diagonalizes the original two-component laboratory Hamiltonian and measures the bare diagonal kinetic operator through its eigenvectors. Its inverse-gap extrapolation does not use the oracle connection or scalar correction. The extra unsplit laboratory Fourier-matrix checks independently test the sector indexing.
Bare kinetic energy and total energy plus Delta agree in the requested limiting state, not generally at finite Delta. The public readout and reference retain this distinction.

The completed shortcut is a consistent positive scalar rotor Hamiltonian with the correct local scalar correction, but ordinary integer scalar sectors. It misses the internal-state holonomy fixed by the full periodic laboratory spinor.

Even q at theta=pi/2 has an integer connection: relabeling the full angular sum makes the calibration exactly shared despite its nonzero scalar correction. Odd and tilted preparations test fractional sectors with positive kinetic readouts. Zero-texture and integer-gauge limits are consistent.

input_and_grading_review.hidden_coverage: Three nonzero fractional-sector groups and an even-winding anchor group, all within the documented domain. The same output metric applies to all groups.
input_and_grading_review.runtime: Pinned dependencies; agent600s/verifier60s unchanged. Existing local runs finish below .4s.
